provenance.origin: Z3-Datalog (NoD) reachability instances shipped with the dataset, tarred 2013-08-14
provenance.why_it_matters: the only verdicts in this benchmark suite produced OUTSIDE this repository -- every other correctness result here is a consensus between implementations in this tree (AD6_PLAN.md 9.28, TODO.md item 1s)
provenance.smt2_files_not_vendored: 4.6 MB of Datalog left in the source archive; the source/target/constraint of each query is transcribed below and nothing else is read from them
provenance.node_id_convention: CLOUD_BENCH_PLAN.md 1.2 -- even node = transmit side, odd = receive side
provenance.declare_rel_argument_order: (ip_src, ip_dst, tcp_src, tcp_dst, vlan, ip_proto, tcp_ctrl)

queries.name: q01
queries.question: from the internet, unconstrained, can anything reach this host?

queries.name: q02
queries.question: same, for a host that publishes no service

queries.name: q03
queries.question: from the internet on TCP/332, can anything reach this host?

queries.name: q04
queries.question: from the internet on ANY port other than 331, can anything reach this host?

queries.name: q05
queries.question: host to host across datacenters, on a permitted service port

queries.name: q06
queries.question: the same pair one port over -- isolates the ACL from the forwarding

open_discrepancy: cloud-tf/README.txt says the public TCP port is 331, and q04 excludes 331 consistently with that -- but q03 is SATISFIABLE on port 332. Settle this before attributing any FaVe/oracle mismatch to FaVe: an off-by-one in a port number is exactly the shape of defect that manufactures a false disagreement. See CLOUD_BENCH_PLAN.md 1.4.
